questions.q: The path was very narrow. Two people could not walk side by side. **(too)**
questions.m: The path was too narrow for two people to walk side by side

questions.q: He forgot his password. He could not log in. **(Because)**
questions.m: Because he forgot his password, he could not log in

questions.q: "I have never been to Japan," my aunt said. **(Begin: My aunt said …)**
questions.m: My aunt said that she had never been to Japan

questions.q: Someone is cleaning the windows now. **(Begin: The windows …)**
questions.m: The windows are being cleaned now

questions.q: The girl won the scholarship. Her essay was outstanding. **(whose)**
questions.m: The girl whose essay was outstanding won the scholarship

questions.q: It rained heavily. The football match was abandoned. **(As a result of)**
questions.m: As a result of the heavy rain, the football match was abandoned

questions.q: He is short. He cannot reach the top shelf. **(enough)**
questions.m: He is not tall enough to reach the top shelf

questions.q: The teacher entered. The class stopped talking immediately. **(The moment)**
questions.m: The moment the teacher entered, the class stopped talking

questions.q: "Switch off your phones," the usher told the audience. **(Begin: The usher told …)**
questions.m: The usher told the audience to switch off their phones

questions.q: She has a talent for drawing. She also writes well. **(not only)**
questions.m: She is not only talented at drawing but also writes well
questions.tip: Also accept: Not only does she have a talent for drawing, but she also writes well.

questions.q: We arrived at the cinema. The film had already begun. **(By the time)**
questions.m: By the time we arrived at the cinema, the film had already begun

questions.q: Nobody in the choir has a better voice than Amira. **(Begin: Amira has …)**
questions.m: Amira has the best voice in the choir

questions.q: He saved his pocket money. He bought a telescope. **(By)**
questions.m: By saving his pocket money, he bought a telescope

questions.q: It is expensive to live in the city centre. **(Begin: Living …)**
questions.m: Living in the city centre is expensive

questions.q: You must wear a helmet. You will not be allowed to cycle otherwise. **(Unless)**
questions.m: Unless you wear a helmet, you will not be allowed to cycle

questions.q: The soup was extremely hot. I burnt my tongue. **(so … that)**
questions.m: The soup was so hot that I burnt my tongue

questions.q: They have not announced the results yet. **(Begin: The results …)**
questions.m: The results have not been announced yet

questions.q: He only apologised after his mother spoke to him. **(It was not until)**
questions.m: It was not until his mother spoke to him that he apologised

questions.q: My brother dislikes crowds. I dislike crowds too. **(Neither)**
questions.m: Neither my brother nor I like crowds
questions.tip: Verb agrees with the nearer subject.

questions.q: The children were excited. They could not sleep. **(too)**
questions.m: The children were too excited to sleep

questions.q: She left early. She wanted to avoid the rain. **(so that)**
questions.m: She left early so that she could avoid the rain

questions.q: "Why are you late again?" the teacher asked Ravi. **(Begin: The teacher asked Ravi …)**
questions.m: The teacher asked Ravi why he was late again
questions.tip: Statement word order in reported questions.

questions.q: The performance was excellent. The audience gave a standing ovation. **(such)**
questions.m: It was such an excellent performance that the audience gave a standing ovation

questions.q: He lost his temper. He regretted it immediately. **(No sooner)**
questions.m: No sooner had he lost his temper than he regretted it

questions.q: The road is closed. We cannot reach the beach. **(prevents)**
questions.m: The closed road prevents us from reaching the beach

questions.q: She began learning the erhu five years ago. **(Begin: She has …)**
questions.m: She has been learning the erhu for five years

questions.q: The instructions were unclear. We still assembled the shelf correctly. **(Although)**
questions.m: Although the instructions were unclear, we still assembled the shelf correctly

questions.q: The instructions were unclear. We still assembled the shelf correctly. **(In spite of)**
questions.m: In spite of the unclear instructions, we still assembled the shelf correctly

questions.q: People say that this bridge is the oldest in the country. **(Begin: This bridge …)**
questions.m: This bridge is said to be the oldest in the country

questions.q: He prefers walking to taking the bus. **(would rather)**
questions.m: He would rather walk than take the bus

questions.q: The shop was closed. We could not buy the tickets. **(Because of)**
questions.m: Because of the closed shop, we could not buy the tickets

questions.q: "Let's tidy the classroom together," said the monitor. **(Begin: The monitor suggested …)**
questions.m: The monitor suggested tidying the classroom together
questions.tip: Also accept: suggested that we should tidy…

questions.q: This is the café. We first met here. **(where)**
questions.m: This is the café where we first met

questions.q: He is accustomed to waking at five. **(used to)**
questions.m: He is used to waking at five

questions.q: The bag was heavy. The handle snapped. **(so … that)**
questions.m: The bag was so heavy that the handle snapped

questions.q: Hardly anyone attended. The organisers were disappointed. **(Since)**
questions.m: Since hardly anyone attended, the organisers were disappointed

questions.q: Both the coach and the players were pleased. **(not only … but also)**
questions.m: Not only the coach but also the players were pleased

questions.q: The vase is priceless. It was made in the Ming dynasty. **(which)**
questions.m: The vase, which was made in the Ming dynasty, is priceless

questions.q: I did not recognise him. He had grown a beard. **(because)**
questions.m: I did not recognise him because he had grown a beard

questions.q: She spoke very quietly. Nobody at the back heard her. **(too)**
questions.m: She spoke too quietly for anybody at the back to hear her

questions.q: Nobody had told him. He arrived at the wrong venue. **(Having)**
questions.m: Having been told by nobody, he arrived at the wrong venue
questions.tip: Also accept: Not having been told, he arrived at the wrong venue.

questions.q: The lift broke down twice last week. Nobody has repaired it. **(despite)**
questions.m: The lift has not been repaired despite breaking down twice last week

questions.q: "Do not feed the monkeys," the ranger warned the visitors. **(Begin: The ranger warned …)**
questions.m: The ranger warned the visitors not to feed the monkeys

questions.q: The homework was difficult. My father could not help me. **(so … that)**
questions.m: The homework was so difficult that even my father could not help me

questions.q: No other museum in the city is as popular as this one. **(Begin: This museum …)**
questions.m: This museum is the most popular in the city

questions.q: He practised daily. He still did not qualify. **(Even though)**
questions.m: Even though he practised daily, he still did not qualify

questions.q: Someone had left the tap running all night. **(Begin: The tap …)**
questions.m: The tap had been left running all night

questions.q: The queue moved slowly. We waited for two hours. **(such)**
questions.m: It was such a slow queue that we waited for two hours

questions.q: She checked the answers twice. She wanted to avoid careless mistakes. **(in order to)**
questions.m: She checked the answers twice in order to avoid careless mistakes

questions.q: "Can you help me carry this?" my neighbour asked. **(Begin: My neighbour asked …)**
questions.m: My neighbour asked me to help her carry that

Neither the cups nor the teapot ______ broken.

Please remind me ______ the library books.
The scissors ______ in the top drawer.
By this time next year, she ______ in Australia for a decade.
He speaks English ______ well ______ his sister.
Very few pupils ______ able to answer the last question.
The museum is closed on Mondays, ______?
We were made ______ the whole exercise again.
Everybody ______ brought their own lunch today.
He denied ______ anything about the missing money.
The concert was postponed ______ the typhoon warning.
This soup tastes ______ than yesterday's.
She is looking forward ______ her cousins next month.
Not one of the answers ______ correct.
The boys helped ______ to the drinks.
I wish I ______ taller.
He ran out of the house ______ locking the door.

Rarely ______ such generosity from a stranger.
The twins are ______ alike that I cannot tell them apart.
Please hand your form ______ the office before noon.
He is the only one of the boys who ______ able to swim.
They objected ______ the new rule.
Little ______ that his bag had already been found.
The furniture in the new flat ______ arrived yet.
We stayed indoors, ______ the weather forecast had been wrong.
He avoided ______ eye contact with the teacher.
Do you know what time ______?
Three-quarters of the field ______ been flooded.
The hall fell silent as the conductor raised his baton, and the audience waited in __________ anticipation.
questions.tip: 'Eager anticipation' is the usual phrase for excited waiting; a hushed, expectant audience is not 'bored'.

questions.q: Her explanation was so __________ that even the youngest pupils understood it.
After the scandal, the company worked hard to __________ its reputation.
questions.tip: 'Restore' means bring back to its former good state, which is what a damaged reputation needs.

questions.q: The old dog's __________ made the short walk take twenty minutes.
questions.tip: 'Frailty' means weakness, usually from old age, explaining why the short walk took twenty minutes.

questions.q: He is a __________ collector who has every stamp issued since 1965.
questions.tip: 'Meticulous' means extremely careful and thorough, matching a collection missing no stamp since 1965.

questions.q: The committee reached a decision only after a __________ debate lasting four hours.
questions.tip: A 'heated' debate is angry and passionate, which is why the decision took four hours.

questions.q: She accepted the criticism with quiet __________ and promised to improve.
questions.tip: 'Dignity' means calm self-respect; 'resentment' is the trap, but she promised to improve instead.

questions.q: The instructions were __________ in three languages so that nobody would be confused.
questions.tip: Putting words into other languages is 'translating'; 'duplicated' would only repeat the same language.

questions.q: His stomach __________ loudly in the middle of the silent examination hall.
questions.tip: Stomachs 'rumble' — a deep growling noise; the other verbs describe soft, gentle sounds.

questions.q: The witness's story was __________; it changed three times in ten minutes.
questions.tip: 'Inconsistent' means not staying the same, exactly what a story changing three times does.

questions.q: Thick fog __________ the top of the hill from view.
questions.tip: 'Obscured' means hid from view, which is what thick fog does; 'revealed' means the opposite.

questions.q: She has a __________ appetite and can finish a plate meant for two.
questions.tip: A 'hearty' appetite is a big, healthy one, fitting someone who finishes a plate for two.

questions.q: The volunteers were praised for their __________ during the flood.
questions.tip: 'Selflessness' means putting others before yourself, the quality flood volunteers are praised for.

questions.q: He gave a __________ nod, as though he had barely noticed us.
The path had become __________ after weeks of rain, so we turned back.
questions.tip: 'Treacherous' means dangerously slippery and unsafe, which is why weeks of rain made them turn back.

questions.q: The child's questions were endless, but her mother answered each one with __________.
questions.tip: 'Patience' means staying calm without getting annoyed, which endless questions really test.

questions.q: After the argument, an uneasy __________ settled over the household.
questions.tip: A 'truce' is an agreed pause in quarrelling, fitting the uneasy calm after an argument.

questions.q: The magician's movements were so __________ that nobody saw the switch.
He is __________ about his diet and will not touch anything fried.
questions.tip: 'Fastidious' means very fussy and particular, which is why he refuses anything fried.

questions.q: Her first attempt was __________, but by the fifth she was competent.
questions.tip: 'But' contrasts with 'competent', so her first attempt was 'dismal' — thoroughly poor.

questions.q: The hikers were __________ when they finally saw the shelter through the trees.
questions.tip: 'Elated' means overjoyed, the natural feeling when tired hikers finally spot their shelter.

questions.q: He spoke with such __________ that the whole class believed him instantly.
questions.tip: 'Conviction' means firm, sure belief, and speaking with it is what made the class believe him.

questions.q: The soil here is __________, which is why nothing grows well.
questions.tip: 'Barren' soil grows nothing; 'fertile' and 'rich' are traps meaning the very opposite.

questions.q: She made a __________ recovery and was back at school within a week.
questions.tip: 'Remarkable' means surprisingly good, fitting a recovery quick enough to return within a week.

questions.q: The crowd dispersed __________ once the announcement was made.
questions.tip: 'Once the announcement was made' points to a sudden response.

questions.q: His handwriting is __________ small; I need a magnifying glass.
questions.tip: 'Impossibly' means to an unbelievable degree, the only word strong enough for needing a magnifying glass.

questions.q: The teacher's __________ tone left nobody in any doubt about the deadline.
questions.tip: A 'firm' tone is decided and leaves no doubt, while hesitant or uncertain tones create doubt.

questions.q: They made a __________ attempt to repair the fence, and it collapsed again the next day.
questions.tip: 'Half-hearted' means done without real effort, which explains why the fence collapsed the next day.

questions.q: The chef sampled the sauce and added a __________ of salt.
questions.tip: A 'pinch' is the tiny amount held between finger and thumb, the right measure for seasoning.

questions.q: After three hours of revision, my concentration began to __________.
The two accounts of the accident were completely __________.
questions.tip: 'Contradictory' means the two accounts say opposite things, so they cannot both be true.

questions.q: The little boy clung to his mother, __________ of the strangers in the room.
questions.tip: 'Wary of' means cautious and distrustful of, which is why he clung to his mother.

questions.q: The award was a fitting __________ of thirty years of service.
questions.tip: 'Recognition' means honouring what somebody has done, which is what an award for long service is.

questions.q: She is __________ punctual; in five years she has never once been late.
questions.tip: 'Invariably' means always, without exception, matching five years without a single late arrival.

questions.q: The room was __________ furnished — a bed, a chair and nothing else.
questions.tip: 'Sparsely' means with very little, matching a room holding only a bed and a chair.

questions.q: He __________ the blame rather than let his teammate be punished.
questions.tip: To 'shoulder' blame is to take it on yourself, which saves the teammate from punishment.

questions.q: The scent of the durian was __________ and filled the entire lift.
questions.tip: 'Overpowering' means so strong that it overwhelms you, fitting a smell that filled a whole lift.

questions.q: Their friendship __________ over many years of shared hardship.
questions.tip: 'Deepened' means grew stronger, the natural result of many years of shared hardship.

questions.q: The manager's decision was __________; no appeal would be considered.
questions.tip: 'Final' means settled and unchangeable, which is why no appeal would be considered.

questions.q: A __________ of pigeons scattered as the child ran through the square.
questions.tip: Birds gather in a 'flock'; 'herd' suits cattle, 'pack' wolves and 'school' fish.

questions.q: She dismissed the rumour as __________ nonsense.
questions.tip: 'Utter' means complete, and 'utter nonsense' is the usual phrase for something wholly untrue.

questions.q: The road was __________ with potholes after the long monsoon.
questions.tip: 'Riddled with' means full of, especially holes, so it suits a road covered in potholes.

questions.q: He made a __________ effort to be friendly, but nobody was fooled.
questions.tip: A token effort is done only for appearance.

questions.q: The lecture was informative but delivered in a __________ monotone.
questions.tip: 'Dreary' means dull and dispiriting, the only word that suits an unchanging monotone.

questions.q: The referee's decision provoked __________ from both sets of supporters.
questions.tip: Only 'outrage' — furious anger — explains a decision that upset both sets of supporters at once.

questions.q: My grandmother's advice proved __________ when I faced the same problem years later.
questions.tip: 'Invaluable' means extremely useful, which good advice proves to be when it solves a later problem.

questions.q: The kitten's __________ curiosity led it into the open cupboard.
questions.tip: 'Insatiable' means never satisfied, and only such strong curiosity would lead the kitten inside.

questions.q: He answered every question __________, without once consulting his notes.
questions.tip: Answering without once checking his notes shows he was sure of himself, which 'confidently' means.

questions.q: The flood left a thick __________ of mud across the entire car park.
questions.tip: A 'layer' is a flat covering spread over a surface, which is how mud settles after flooding.

questions.q: She is far too __________ to boast about coming first.
questions.tip: 'Modest' means not boastful, the only word that makes 'far too ... to boast' sensible.

questions.q: Passage 7 — Last December, my family and I flew to Taipei for a week-long holidays.
questions.m: holiday
questions.tip: The error was “holidays”. 'A week-long' needs the singular.

questions.q: Passage 7 — We stay in a small hotel close to the night market.
questions.m: stayed
questions.tip: The error was “stay”. The account is in the past tense.

questions.q: Passage 7 — The rooms was tiny, but they were spotlessly clean.
questions.m: were

questions.q: Passage 7 — On the first evening, we walk through the market for nearly three hours.
questions.m: walked

questions.q: Passage 7 — My brother ate so much that he complained of a stomachache afterward.
questions.m: afterwards
questions.tip: The error was “afterward”. In British and Singapore usage, 'afterwards'.

questions.q: Passage 7 — The next day we visited a temple who was more than two hundred years old.
questions.m: which
questions.tip: The error was “who”. A temple is a thing.

questions.q: Passage 7 — My mother was fascinated with the carvings on the wooden doors.
questions.m: by

questions.q: Passage 7 — Unfortunately, it rained heavy on our last two days.
questions.m: heavily
questions.tip: The error was “heavy”. It describes how it rained.

questions.q: Passage 7 — We spent those afternoons in a bookshop, where we drank tea and reading.
questions.m: read
questions.tip: The error was “reading”. It must match 'drank'.

questions.q: Passage 7 — I have decided that I will definately return one day.
questions.m: definitely
questions.tip: The error was “definately”. Spelling — definite + ly.

questions.q: Passage 8 — Our class was ask to design a poster for Racial Harmony Day.
questions.m: asked
questions.tip: The error was “ask”. Passive needs the past participle.

questions.q: Passage 8 — Mrs Goh divided us into five group of six pupils each.
questions.m: groups

questions.q: Passage 8 — Every group were given a large sheet of paper and a box of markers.
questions.m: was
questions.tip: The error was “were”. 'Every group' is singular.

questions.q: Passage 8 — My group decided to draw childrens from different backgrounds holding hands.
questions.m: children
questions.tip: The error was “childrens”. 'Children' is already plural.

questions.q: Passage 8 — Nadia, who draws beautiful, sketched the outline first.
questions.m: beautifully
questions.tip: The error was “beautiful”. It describes how she draws.

questions.q: Passage 8 — The rest of us colour it in while she added the lettering.
questions.m: coloured

questions.q: Passage 8 — We work quickly because we only had forty minutes.
questions.m: worked

questions.q: Passage 8 — Our poster was choosen to be displayed at the school entrance.
questions.m: chosen
questions.tip: The error was “choosen”. Spelling — the past participle of 'choose' is 'chosen'.

questions.q: Passage 8 — Mrs Goh said she was very proud in all of us.
questions.m: of

questions.q: Passage 8 — It was the first time our group had ever won anything.
questions.m: won
questions.tip: This line is correct as written — but the grammar here is worth noting.

questions.q: Passage 9 — My neighbour keeps four cats, and each of them have a different name.
questions.m: has

questions.q: Passage 9 — The oldest one, Biscuit, is almost fiveteen years old.
questions.m: fifteen

questions.q: Passage 9 — He sleeps on the window ledge for most of the day, hardly ever move.
questions.m: moving
questions.tip: The error was “move”. It must match 'sleeps' as a participle phrase.

questions.q: Passage 9 — Last month, my neighbour ask me to feed them while she was away.
questions.m: asked

questions.q: Passage 9 — She left detailed instruction taped to the refrigerator door.
questions.m: instructions
questions.tip: The error was “instruction”. 'Detailed' here needs the plural.

questions.q: Passage 9 — On the first morning, only three cats appeared, which worry me greatly.
questions.m: worried

questions.q: Passage 9 — I searched every room but could not found Biscuit anywhere.
questions.m: find
questions.tip: The error was “found”. After 'could', use the base form.

questions.q: Passage 9 — Finally I heared a faint scratching from inside the laundry basket.
questions.m: heard
questions.tip: The error was “heared”. The past tense of 'hear' is 'heard'.

questions.q: Passage 9 — He had fell asleep among the towels and refused to come out.
questions.m: fallen
questions.tip: The error was “fell”. After 'had', use the past participle.

questions.q: Passage 9 — I was so relief that I sat on the floor and laughed.
questions.m: relieved
questions.tip: The error was “relief”. It describes how I felt.

passages.text:
The Lost Library Card

For two weeks I told nobody that I had lost my library card. I kept hoping it (1)______ turn up in a pocket or at the bottom of my bag, and every evening I searched the same three places (2)______ finding it.

The problem was that I (3)______ (borrow) six books on it the week before. If somebody found the card and used it, the books would still be recorded (4)______ my name.

In the end my father noticed that I had stopped going to the library, (5)______ was unusual. When he asked why, I told him everything.

He did not scold me. He simply said that a problem kept secret (6)______ always larger than a problem shared, and then he drove me to the library, (7)______ the librarian cancelled the old card and issued a new one in under four minutes.

It cost two dollars. I had spent a fortnight worrying about something that (8)______ have been solved on the first day.

Since (9)______, I have kept the card in the same pocket of the same bag. I have also learnt to tell my father about a problem (10)______ it becomes a fortnight old.

The School Rabbit

Every class in our school looks after the rabbit for one term, and this year it (11)______ (be) our turn. Mrs Menon warned us on the first day that Pepper was older than most of us realised and needed (12)______ handled gently.

We drew up a roster (13)______ that everybody had a turn at feeding him. Two pupils were on duty each morning, and (14)______ pupils were responsible for cleaning the hutch on Fridays.

At first there was a great deal of enthusiasm. (15)______ the third week, however, the novelty had worn off, and I noticed that the same two people were doing most of the work.

Mrs Menon did not remind us. She simply pinned the roster (16)______ the noticeboard with the completed duties ticked off in green, and the empty ones left blank. (17)______ anybody said anything, the blanks began to fill in.

By the end of term, Pepper (18)______ (gain) a little weight and his coat looked better (19)______ it had in September. The class next door took over in April.

I still check on him at recess sometimes, (20)______ it is no longer my responsibility.

answers.tip: Refers back to the whole situation.
Refers to the library, a place.
Tell him before it becomes old.
'Needed to be handled' or 'needed being handled' — 'to' is expected.
A different pair had the Friday duty.
'Without anybody saying' would need a gerund, so 'Before' fits the clause.
Completed by the end of term.

passages.text:
The Handwriting Book

When my mother was seven, her teacher made the whole class copy out a page of cursive every afternoon for a year. She still describes it as the most (1)______ year of her schooling. She also has, to this day, the most beautiful handwriting of anyone I have ever met.

I mention this because last month I found a thin exercise book at the bottom of a drawer, and inside it, page after page, was my own name written out in my mother's hand — the same three words, hundreds of (2)______ over.

I did not understand at first. Then I saw the date on the cover: the year I was six, which was the year I was struggling so badly with writing that my teacher had suggested I be (3)______ for extra support.

My mother had taught herself how to teach me. She had written out my name in different sizes, first large and (4)______ , then smaller, so that I could trace over the top. Every page was a slightly harder (5)______ than the one before.

I have no memory of any of this. None. I remember learning to write the way you remember learning to walk — which is to say, not at (6)______ .

When I showed her the book, she looked (7)______ it for a while and said, "Oh, that old thing," and then went back to what she was doing. She is not a woman who enjoys being (8)______ .

But I have thought about it a great deal since. It must have taken her several hours a week for months. She was working full time. She never (9)______ me it was happening, and she certainly never expected me to (10)______ it thirty years later in a drawer.

My own handwriting is (11)______ — nobody would describe it as beautiful. But it is legible, and it has been legible since I was seven, and I now know exactly (12)______ .

There is a thing people say about parents, which is that you only understand them once you have children of your (13)______ . I do not think that is quite right. I think you understand them the first time you find the (14)______ of something they did quietly and never mentioned.

The exercise book is on my desk now. I have not told her I (15)______ it.

The Reservoir at Six

My father has run around the same reservoir at six in the morning, four days a week, for as long as I can (16)______ . He is sixty-three. The loop is eight kilometres and he has never, in my hearing, described it as enjoyable.

When I was fourteen I asked him why he kept doing something he did not (17)______ . He said that enjoyment was not the point, which struck me at the time as a thoroughly (18)______ answer and struck me later as the most useful thing he ever told me.

Last year he had an operation on his knee and was told not to run for four (19)______ . I expected him to be miserable. Instead he walked the loop. Slowly, badly, with a stick for the first fortnight, but he walked it, four mornings a week, at the same (20)______ .

I asked him whether walking counted.

"It is not about the running," he said. "It is about being the person who (21)______ up."

I have never been able to keep a habit going for more than about three (22)______ . I start things with tremendous energy. I read half of a great many books. There is a guitar in my flat that I have played perhaps eleven (23)______ .

What I have finally understood, watching him limp around a reservoir at dawn, is that I have been treating motivation as the (24)______ of the habit, when in fact it is the reward. He does not run because he feels like running. He feels (25)______ because he runs.

This year I started swimming. Twice a week, badly, at a pool near my office. It is not (26)______ , and there have been several mornings when I very nearly did not (27)______ .

But I have kept it up for seven months, which is by a considerable (28)______ the longest I have kept anything.

My father has never asked me about it, and I have never (29)______ it. I think we both understand that talking about a habit is a reliable way of (30)______ it.

answers.tip: She hated it, though it worked.
What a teacher suggests for a struggling pupil.
Each page was a little harder.
The exercise book is physical evidence.
He has not told her he has it.
A fourteen-year-old would find it inadequate.
Contrast with 'reward' in the same sentence.
'He feels like it because he runs.' Accept 'better'.
Talking about it tends to end it.
